lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Add a clear target-position descriptor near your name or contact information.
items.because: A recruiter should understand your intended direction immediately.

items.says: LinkedIn URL looks like a placeholder or generic website.
items.because: example.com/in/riley-chen currently looks like a placeholder or generic website.

items.says: Consider adding location or work authorization if relevant.
items.because: This helps clarify your fit for target roles.

items.says: Make the MBA status clear if it is completed rather than ongoing.
items.because: Leaving the date range without a completion indicator can create unnecessary uncertainty.

items.says: Add a concentration, relevant coursework, leadership role, award, or academic distinction only if it is genuinely relevant and strong.
items.because: The MBA should support the product/operations narrative rather than function as a standalone credential.

items.says: Consider whether the MBA should appear before experience if you are applying for entry-level or MBA-targeted product roles.
items.because: Section order should support your target narrative.

items.says: Remove the location if space becomes necessary.
items.because: Space can be saved for more relevant content.

items.says: Do not add additional detail unless you have a directly relevant distinction, coursework, or leadership credential.
items.because: Your professional experience is stronger evidence.

items.says: Reduce the amount of space devoted to the Diesel Mechanic role unless the target role values field operations, industrial systems, asset management, reliability, or hands-on technical work.
items.because: A recruiter may see 'Diesel Mechanic' after an MBA and assume you are changing direction away from product or business roles.

items.says: Clarify the scale and ownership of the work.
items.because: The operational consequence of the five-day dry-dock result is unclear.

items.says: Make the operational consequence of the five-day dry-dock result easier to understand.
items.because: The reader may not know whether the five-day figure represents improvement, a required standard, or merely the normal job duration.

items.says: Confirm that 'under 5 days per job' is a repeatable performance level rather than an isolated best case.
items.because: The metric's meaning is ambiguous.

items.says: Add volume, reliability, turnaround, safety, or downtime context if accurate.
items.because: Business impact needs to be evident.

items.says: Decide whether this bullet is worth keeping for the target roles.
items.because: It is less relevant to product roles than other bullets.

items.says: Emphasize the operational, compliance, asset-management, or documentation dimension rather than listing maintenance tasks.
items.because: Responsibility statements are weaker than measurable results.

items.because: Scope and impact are unclear.

items.says: Add the scale of the scorecards: number of carriers, regions, shipments, managers, or metrics.
items.because: Scale is missing.

items.says: Clarify what decisions or changes resulted from the reporting.

items.says: Replace responsibility-only framing with evidence of business impact if you have it.

items.says: Identify whether you built the reporting process, improved it, or merely administered it.
items.because: Ownership and initiative are unclear.

items.says: Add the baseline or operational consequence if available, such as error volume, customer impact, labor cost, or returns.
items.because: Measurement context is missing.

items.says: Clarify your role relative to the supervisors: analysis, design, implementation, training, or all four.
items.because: Your contribution is not fully clear.

items.says: Check whether the 30% reduction was measured over a defined period.
items.because: The period of measurement is not specified.

items.says: Make the size and business importance of the forecast clearer if possible.
items.because: Business impact is not fully explained.

items.says: Clarify whether you created the consensus method or facilitated its adoption.
items.because: The distinction between 'introduced' and 'designed and implemented' matters.

items.because: Analytical readers may want more detail.

items.says: Separate or clarify the different responsibilities: implementation, change management, training, and vendor management.

items.says: Explain how the 1,800-hour saving was calculated.
items.because: The calculation method is not given.

items.says: Clarify your level of ownership in the vendor negotiation.
items.because: Boundaries of your contribution should be clear.

items.says: Add financial impact if the hours can be translated into cost, capacity, or service improvement.
items.because: Financial impact would strengthen the claim.

items.because: Section order should highlight the most relevant achievements.

items.says: Group related onboarding bullets together and related experimentation bullets together.
items.because: Grouping reduces repetition and clarifies scope.

items.says: Remove or consolidate bullets that describe the same project from different angles.

items.says: Make sure the section does not look inflated for a ten-week internship.
items.because: Six bullets for a short internship can seem overstated.

items.says: Confirm whether the reduction was measured against a comparable pre-launch cohort.

items.because: Wording needs precision.

items.says: Explain whether 'all merchants' means all merchants in the pilot region or the company’s entire merchant base.
items.because: Scope is ambiguous.

items.says: Avoid implying that the post-test rollout produced the same result unless that was measured.

items.says: Keep only if you can show the decision or outcome that resulted.
